name: Old Town of Segovia and its Aqueduct
description: In the Spanish city of Segovia, a Roman aqueduct of 167 arches strides across the town in two tiers, built around AD 50 and still standing. It carried spring water from mountains 17 kilometres away and stayed in use until 1973. Around it, the old town climbs to the fairy-tale Alcázar, begun in the 11th century, and a 16th-century Gothic cathedral.
